Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:9: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Peah ch. 1, mishnah 1): these are the things a person enjoys the fruits of in this world, while the principal remains for him in the World to Come, and so on, and Torah study is equal to all of them; and moreover, one who occupies himself with Torah study is exempt from all the commandments, for it is weighed as equal to all the commandments:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:10: And it was taught in the school of Elijah, of blessed memory (Avodah Zarah 5b), happy is the person who makes himself like an ox to the yoke and like a donkey to its burden, and sits and reads and reviews Torah continually every day, and immediately the Holy Spirit rests upon him; and if one who merely sits idle is punished so severely, how much more so one who actually mocks:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:11: Idle talk leads to grave transgressions, for even one who merely sits idle, this is called a "session of scoffers," and is punished with great punishments, as mentioned above regarding mockery — how much more so one who actually speaks idle talk, and moreover it leads to evil speech, gossip-mongering, mockery, and speaking of one's fellow's disgrace:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:12: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 19b), whoever speaks idle talk transgresses a positive commandment, as it is said (Deuteronomy 6:7), "and you shall speak of them"; and they said of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai (Sukkah 28a) and of Rav (Rambam, ch. 2 of the laws of...), that in all their days they never spoke idle chatter; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot ch. 1, mishnah 17), I have found nothing better for the body than silence, and it is written (Micah 3:28), "let him sit alone and be silent... let him put his mouth to the dust," and it is written (Proverbs 18:21), "death and life are in the hand of the tongue," and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot ch. 3, mishnah 13), a fence for wisdom is silence, and Solomon said (Ecclesiastes 5:1), "Do not be rash with your mouth, and let not your heart hasten to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on the earth; therefore let your words be few":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:13: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Chullin 89), "Do you indeed speak righteousness, you mute ones?" (Psalms 58:2) — what is a person's craft in this world? He should make himself mute; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Chagigah 23a), when Rebbi would reach this verse he would weep (Amos 4:13), "for behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what is his speech" — even the casual conversation a person has with his wife, and even matters of no substance, are written in a person's ledger and read before him at the time of his death:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:14: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said, a person's silence brings him to humility, and humility is the beginning of the fear of Heaven, and when he is not occupying himself with Torah he should be silent and press his lips together like two millstones lying one atop the other, for a person's righteous deeds and merits are never sufficient to justify what he lets out with his lips; happy is he who makes himself mute, deaf, lame, and blind — and why all this? So that he not sin and thereby render himself and his limbs liable to Gehinnom; and so David says (Psalms 31:11), "but I am like a deaf man, I do not hear, and like a mute who does not open his mouth":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:15: And in Sefer HaZohar (II, 59a): there is no breath that does not have a sound, and all those words in which a person occupies himself that are not for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He — that word becomes a breath (hevel) that roams about the world, and when his soul departs, that breath sends him roaming about the world, and this is [the meaning of] (I Samuel 25:29), "and the souls of your enemies He will sling out from the hollow of a sling"; and it is said there (III, 183b), "and Esther put on royalty" — we have learned from here that whoever guards his mouth and his tongue merits to be clothed in the Holy Spirit:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:16: <small>[Translation — There is no breath that does not have a sound, and all those words that a person occupies himself with, which are not for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, that word becomes a breath and roams about the world, and when his soul departs, that breath sends him roaming about the world. And this is what is meant by "and the souls of your enemies He will sling out from the hollow of a sling." And they said there, "and Esther put on royalty" — we learn from here that whoever guards his mouth and his tongue merits to be clothed in the Holy Spirit.]</small>:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:17: One who gazes at forbidden sights, even if he were like Moses himself, hand to hand [i.e., utterly reliable], would not be acquitted from the judgment of Gehinnom; and his end is to sin in forbidden relations, for he stirs up the evil inclination within himself, and comes to a grave form of seminal emission, as will be explained in Gate Six:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:18: One who benefits from the honor of the Torah takes his own life from the world and makes himself liable for his own soul, and the incident of Rabbi Tarfon proves this (Nedarim 62a) — that they would throw him into the river to kill him, yet he did not wish to benefit from words of Torah — as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot ch. 4, mishnah 5), "do not make them a crown to magnify yourself with, nor an axe [to earn your living]," and so on, for whoever benefits from the honor of the Torah takes his own life from the world, and his end is to inherit Gehinnom:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:19: Falsehood: one who speaks lies denies the God of Israel and, as it were, acknowledges a different god, which is falsehood; and he is of the class that does not see the face of the Shechinah, as it is written (Psalms 101:7), "he who speaks lies shall not be established before My eyes," and he is not included among Israel, of whom it is written (Zephaniah 3:13), "the remnant of Israel shall do no iniquity nor speak falsehood," and his days are shortened,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:20: but one who speaks truth lives long, as they said in Massekhet Sanhedrin (97a) regarding Rav Tavyomi, that even if they gave him all the treasures of the world, he would not deviate in his speech. Once he happened upon a place called Kushta (Truth), where they never deviated in their speech, and no person there ever died before his time, and so on; two of his sons died there. They said to him, "we beg of you, leave this place, and do not bring death upon us."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:21: And it is written (Jeremiah 9:4), "they have taught their tongue to speak lies... shall I not punish them for these things, says the Lord? Shall My soul not take vengeance on such a nation as this?"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:22: And the spies and the generation of the wilderness were punished only because of false testimony, and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 92a), whoever deviates in his speech is as though he worshipped idols, and it is written (Proverbs 6:16), "there are six things the Lord hates..." — "haughty eyes, a lying tongue... a speaker of falsehoods," and it is written (Psalms 34:13), "who is the man who desires life... guard your tongue from evil":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:23: Gehazi was banished only because he lied in the name of Elisha; Amnon lied to Tamar and was killed; the spirit of Naboth was banished from its place for having spoken falsely, as it is said (I Kings 22:20), "who shall entice Ahab..." — "go out, get out of your place"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:24: And Rav Huna said, Israel was exiled from its land only because they transgressed the verse (Exodus 23:7), "keep far from a false matter"; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 119b, Chagigah 14b), Jerusalem was destroyed only because those of faith ceased from it, as it is said (Jeremiah 5:1), "roam through the streets of Jerusalem..."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:25: And in Sefer HaZohar, at the time falsehood — which is Samael — rules, it is written (Daniel 8:12), "and it cast truth to the ground." And this caused the destruction of the First and Second Temples.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:26: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot ch. 1, mishnah 18), on three things the world stands: on justice, on truth, and on peace, and it is written (Psalms 15:1), "Lord, who shall dwell in Your tent..." and "speaks truth in his heart" — even what he thinks in his heart he must make true through action, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the incident of Rav Safra; and it is written (Malachi 2:6), "the law of truth was in his mouth, and no injustice was found on his lips, for he is a messenger of the Lord of Hosts":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:27: Flattery is among the four classes that do not receive the presence of the Shechinah, since it belittles the honor of the Omnipresent by flattering the wicked man, as it is written (Proverbs 24:24), "He who says to the wicked, you are righteous — peoples shall curse him, nations shall execrate him," and even one who flatters someone who is not actually wicked is like one who feels fear of and trusts in a mere man, and it is written (Jeremiah 17:5), "Cursed is the man who trusts in man," and it is written (Job 13:16), "for a flatterer shall not come before Him,"
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:28: and as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 19a) in the incident of King Yannai, whom the Sanhedrin flattered over some minor matter and did not confront him properly at the time of judgment — Gabriel came and struck them into the ground and they died; and even when they flattered King Agrippa, who was righteous, the enemies of Israel [a euphemism] became liable to destruction:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:29: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 113b), there are three whom the Holy One, blessed be He, hates: one who says one thing with his mouth and another in his heart. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 41b), any person in whom there is flattery falls into Gehinnom, as it is said (Isaiah 5:24), "woe to those who call evil good..." — "therefore, as straw is consumed by a tongue of fire..." And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 42a), any congregation with flattery in it is as loathsome as menstrual impurity, as it is said (Job ch. 5), "for the congregation of the flatterer is desolate"; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 72b), any Torah scholar whose inside is not like his outside is called an abomination,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:30: and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 41b): at the time falsehood — that is, the [Sitra Achra / Satan] — rules, it is written, "and it cast truth to the ground," and this caused the destruction of the First and Second Temples. Any person in whom there is flattery brings anger upon the world, as it is said (ibid. 36), "but the flatterers of heart lay up anger," and moreover his prayer is despised, and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (ibid.), whoever has flattery in him, even the fetuses in their mothers' wombs curse him; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said, for the sin of flattery people fall into the hand of their enemies, as it is said (Isaiah ch. 10), "I will send him against a flattering nation."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:31: Flattery is as grave as idolatry, forbidden sexual relations, and bloodshed. That it is as grave as idolatry — from where do we know this? As it is said (Isaiah ch. 32), "to practice flattery and to speak error against the Lord." That it is as grave as forbidden sexual relations — from where? As it is said (Jeremiah ch. 3), "if a man sends away his wife... will not the land be greatly flattered/defiled?" That it is as grave as bloodshed — from where? As it is said (Psalms ch. 106), "and the land was polluted with blood."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:32: And for the sin of flattery the rains are withheld. And for the sin of flattery one is judged in Gehinnom for all eternity, as it is said (Isaiah ch. 33), "the sinners in Zion are afraid, trembling has seized the flatterers — who among us can dwell with the devouring fire..." and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 101b), Jeroboam did not merit the kingdom except because he did not flatter Solomon:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:33: Deceit contains two great evils: the first, that it is in the category of falsehood and flattery; and the second, that it is in the category of theft and fraud, and it belittles the blessed Name, as if, God forbid, the Holy One, blessed be He, did not recognize his deceit. And it is written (Leviticus 25:17), "and you shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your God," and it is written (ibid. 19), "you shall do no injustice... I am the Lord your God." And a person's judgment after his passing begins with whether he conducted his business dealings faithfully.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:34: It is one of the four classes that do not receive the presence of the Shechinah, as it is said (Psalms ch. 101), "he who practices deceit shall not dwell within my house," and Jerusalem was destroyed only because those of faith ceased from it, as mentioned above regarding falsehood. And it is written (Psalms ch. 15), "Lord, who shall dwell in Your tent..." and "speaks truth in his heart."
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 5:35: And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Midrash Mishlei ch. 28), "a man of faithfulness has abundant blessings" — this is one who conducts his business dealings faithfully, whose possessions increase and for whom the Holy One, blessed be He, provides his sustenance; and moreover he is called a tzaddik, as it is said (Habakkuk 2:4), "and the righteous shall live by his faith"; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Makkot 24b), there are 613 commandments, and so on, and Habakkuk came and established them all upon one: "and the righteous shall live by his faith":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:1-3: On the punishment for negative commandments:

The desecration of the Name is more grave than all transgressions, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 86a) regarding the four categories of atonement: if one transgressed by desecrating the Name, neither repentance, nor Yom Kippur, nor sufferings atone, but only the day of death, as it is said (Isaiah 22:14), "surely this iniquity shall not be atoned for you until you die":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:4: Niddah, apart from its being punishable by karet, they said in Sefer HaZohar (Exodus, 3a): there are three that push the Shechinah away from the world, and people cry out but their voice is not heard, and these are they: niddah, since there is no impurity in the world stronger than the impurity of niddah:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:5: <small>[Translation — There are three that push the Shechinah away from the world, and people cry out but their voice is not heard, and these are they: niddah, because there is no impurity in the world stronger than the impurity of niddah.]</small>:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:6: The Sabbath, it is known, is weighed as equal to all the commandments, and all the wicked have rest on the Sabbath and the fire of Gehinnom is quenched by it, yet the guilt of those who desecrate the Sabbath, "their fire shall not be quenched" even on the Sabbath; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 118b), had Israel kept two Sabbaths properly, they would have been redeemed immediately; and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (ibid.), whoever observes the Sabbath, even if he worships idols like the generation of Enosh, is forgiven, as it is said (Isaiah 56), "happy is the man who does this..." "who keeps the Sabbath from desecrating it," and it is written (Isaiah 58:13), "if you turn your foot away from the Sabbath..." "then you shall delight in the Lord," and so on:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:7: Forbidden fat and blood, it is known, are subject to karet and are things that make the soul detestable:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:8: One who makes improper use of the holy Names — our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Avot chs. 1 and 4), whoever makes use of the crown [of the Torah] shall pass away and be uprooted from the world; either he or his children will apostatize, or he or his children will die, or he or his children will become impoverished:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:9: One who disgraces a Torah scholar, and one who informs [on his fellow Jews to gentile authorities], are among those who have no share in the World to Come and do not arise in the resurrection of the dead:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:10: A wasted seminal emission is worse than the bloodshed of others, and moreover, the blood of that seed and its offspring, without end, is spilled through it; and in Sefer HaZohar, Parashat Vayechi (219b): all sinners have repentance available to them except for this one, and for every other transgression a minor is exempt, except for this one, for Er and Onan, who were minors under the age of seven, died at the hand of Heaven for it — and moreover, they had not yet even been commanded regarding it. And so with the generation of the Flood, of whom it is written, "for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth," and all creatures were dissolved, from man to animal to the birds of the sky and every creeping thing, and even three handbreadths of the soil dissolved — something that had never happened since the world was created, and will never happen again — and moreover, they had been commanded only regarding the seven Noahide laws:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:11: Forbidden foods, it is known, even make the soul detestable, as it is written (Leviticus 21), "and you shall not make your souls detestable," and moreover, one who abstains from them is called holy, as it is written, "you shall not make your souls detestable... and you shall sanctify yourselves... for I am the Lord who brings you up... and you shall be holy, for I am holy"; and you know that holiness brings one to the Holy Spirit:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:12: An oath, whether in vain or false — our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shevuot 39a), at the moment the Holy One, blessed be He, said "You shall not take [My Name in vain]," the whole world trembled; and it is said (Job 9), "who shakes the earth out of its place, and its pillars tremble," and the deep sought to rise up and flood the whole world, and so on. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said, for every other transgression, only the individual is punished, but for this one, he and his family and the whole world are punished, even if the oath was true. Our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Gittin 57a), Yannai had sixty myriad towns on the King's Mountain, and all of them were destroyed on account of an oath, even though it was kept,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 6:13: and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Ketubot 77b) regarding Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, that the Holy One, blessed be He, said: see whether he ever swore an oath and had it annulled through a sage; if so, remove him from the Garden of Eden, and if not, leave him — and they investigated and found that he had never in his life inquired about an oath of his to have it annulled, moreover that he had never sworn an oath in all his days:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 7:1-3: On the fulfillment of positive commandments and the observance of good customs:

Tzitzit — you already know that it is weighed as equal to the whole Torah, and by gematria it is 600, and with its thirteen strands and knots, that makes 613. It is also written, "and you shall see it and remember all the commandments of the Lord," indicating that it is weighed as equal to all the commandments:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 2 7:4: Tefillin — whoever does not fulfill this commandment is called "one whose head has never worn tefillin," and does not arise in the resurrection of the dead. And whoever wears them, all harmful spirits and the nations of the world are afraid of him, and of him it is said (Deuteronomy 28:10), "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you" — Rabbi Elazar says, this refers to the tefillin of the head; and in the future to come, of them it is said (Berachot 17a), "the righteous sit with their crowns on their heads":
